title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
excerpt: Self-hosting LLMs on GPUs means paying to recompute the same context on every turn. Distributed KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache can cut inference cost by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%. This post walks through the distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS, which evaluates and sets up the cache from your coding agent.

ai.summary: The distributed KV caching skill for the AWS Agent Toolkit uses Amazon ElastiCache to cache LLM context, reducing inference cost up to 40% and first‑token latency up to 80%.
ai.why: Developers can lower GPU expenses and speed up self‑hosted LLM applications.

title: Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model
excerpt:
Bytedance and several US universities introduce Axion 1.0, an AI agent that rivals top commercial models from OpenAI and Anthropic on benchmarks after just three training phases. The researchers attribute the gains to carefully curated training data rather than ever more training steps. The model, data, and code are freely available.
The article Bytedance argues most AI training phases are unnecessary and backs it up with a competitive open model appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: Bytedance and partner US universities introduced Axion 1.0, an open‑source AI agent that matches top commercial models on benchmarks after only three curated training phases, and released the model, data, and code publicly.
ai.why: The result challenges the prevailing belief that massive training compute is required for state‑of‑the‑art performance, encouraging more efficient research.

title: New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop
excerpt:
Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, an open looped transformer that runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token. This lets the model reason internally for longer without generating extra text. On Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index, it ties with Qwen3.8 27B at roughly six times lower cost.
The article New open model Inkling 2 Mini thinks in loops to solve problems with fewer words and still runs on a laptop appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Mini, an open‑weight transformer that runs 12 of its 24 layers three times per token, allowing longer internal reasoning while staying laptop‑friendly and about six times cheaper than comparable models on the Intelligence Index.
ai.why: Developers can run a relatively powerful reasoning model locally without cloud costs, enabling new edge‑AI applications.

title: Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft
excerpt:
Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, math's most famous open problem for 167 years, with a proof formalized in Lean that spans over 250,000 pages. Just hours later, Stanford researchers published an independent, entirely human competing proof, and mathematicians are now checking whether either one holds up.
The article Hours after Anthropic claims a Claude proof of the Riemann hypothesis, Stanford releases an all-human competing draft appeared first on The Decoder .

ai.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge reported that Claude produced a Lean formalization of a proof of the Riemann hypothesis spanning more than 250,000 pages, and Stanford released a competing human‑written draft proof hours later.
ai.why: The parallel claims highlight both the potential and the current limits of large language models in deep mathematical reasoning.

title: transformers Release v5.24.0
excerpt:
Release v5.24.0
New Model additions
Inkling 2 Mini
Inkling 2 Mini is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that takes text and images as input and generates text. It is based on Inkling 2 Small, but has 24 decoder layers instead of 48. To make up for the smaller depth, layers 6 to 17 are looped three times, and a learned message-passing mechanism mixes the residuals of the previous pass into the attention and MoE inputs of each loop layer. The decoder routes each token to 8 of 128 experts. A research checkpoint with a variable number of loop passes is also released, so you can trade speed against quality at inference time. ai.summary: Hugging Face Transformers 5.24.0 was released, adding support for Inkling 2 Mini—a 24‑layer multimodal decoder that loops layers 6‑17 three times and routes tokens to 8 of 128 MoE experts.
ai.why: Developers can now load and use Inkling 2 Mini directly through the Transformers library.
